newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 19.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Philippine newspapers - May 19.

text.p: These are the leading stories in Manila newspapers on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- About 2,000 people in Cotabato city, southern Philippines, turned the funeral procession of slain kidnap victim Ching Guan Cue into a protest march against the government's inefficiency in cracking down kidnappers. (INQUIRER)

- The Philippines will assert its claim over the Scarborough Shoal. Government officials vowed to turn the disputed area into a Philippine marine park by pushing for amendments to the military's modernisation programme. (CHRONICLE)
- Manila Archbishop Jaime Cardinal Sin sternly warned priests and bishops on Sunday against endorsing any particular candidate in the 1998 presidential elections. (STAR)
- The trade deficit in the first quarter of 1997 had the slowest rate of expansion in the last five years, records from the National Statistics Office showed. (BUSINESSWORLD)

- The strong performance of the services sector and increasing remittances from overseas will sustain the growth in the economy despite the slowdown in manufacturing, National Economic and Development Authority deputy director general Dante Canlas said. (STANDARD)
- After going through a wild ride last week due to the effect of the falling Thai baht, the Philippine Central Bank expects the domestic financial markets to return to normal this week. (TIMES)
